title: The Sunday Read: 'Jim Dwyer, About New York'

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《Dealbook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的Dealbook峰会上现场采访几位商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的领导人，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zoran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、佐兰·蒙达尼等等。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 届时，您可以观看其中一些毫无保留、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在NYTimes.com上直播部分采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果您还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得一个月的免费阅读权限，畅享我们所有的深度报道。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望您能准时收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 您一定不想错过。

sentences.en: My name is Dan Barry, and I've been a reporter and columnist at the New York Times since forever.
sentences.zh: 我叫丹·巴里，在《纽约时报》担任记者和专栏作家已经很久了。

sentences.en: Today, I'm going to read a few stories by my colleague and friend, Jim Dwyer.
sentences.zh: 今天，我要朗读几篇我的同事兼好友吉姆·德怀尔写的文章。

sentences.en: I knew Jim Dwyer before I knew him because I had read his columns over the years, and I admired his writing and his commitment to justice.
sentences.zh: 在认识吉姆·德怀尔之前，我就已经“认识”他了，因为我多年来一直读他的专栏，我很钦佩他的文笔和他对正义的执着。

sentences.en: Jim's columns often focused on the every person.
sentences.zh: 吉姆的专栏经常聚焦于普通人。

sentences.en: Jim Dwyer, he made a name for himself by writing exclusively about the subways.
sentences.zh: 吉姆·德怀尔，他专门写地铁题材，并因此成名。

sentences.en: He wrote about the people who worked for the subway system, who rode the subways, and he understood more than anyone else how the subways connected the city.
sentences.zh: 他记录了地铁系统的工作人员和乘客，他比任何人都更了解地铁是如何将这座城市连接在一起的。

sentences.en: He would tweak the noses of the powerful, whether it was Mayor Ed Koch, Mayor Dinkins, Mayor Giuliani, Mayor de Blasio, it didn't matter.
sentences.zh: 他会去调侃那些权贵，无论是埃德·科赫市长、丁金斯市长、朱利安尼市长还是白思豪市长，他都一视同仁。

sentences.en: And in 1995, Jim won a Pulitzer Prize for commentary for his columns about New York City.
sentences.zh: 1995年，吉姆凭借关于纽约市的专栏文章获得了普利策评论奖。

sentences.en: The columns at their best were prose poeMs.
sentences.zh: 他最出色的专栏文章简直就是散文诗。

sentences.en: You could smell the apartment or the tenement.
sentences.zh: 你能闻到那间公寓或廉租房的气息。

sentences.en: You could smell the subway.
sentences.zh: 你能闻到地铁的味道。

sentences.en: You were there.
sentences.zh: 仿佛身临其境。

sentences.en: Jim and I had several connections.
sentences.zh: 吉姆和我之间有几个共同点。

sentences.en: For one thing, we were both narrowbacks, which means that we were the children of Irish immigrants.
sentences.zh: 首先，我们都是“窄背”（narrowbacks），意思是我们都是爱尔兰移民的后代。

sentences.en: And the term, which is derogatory to some people, means that you do not have the shoulders as broad as your parents or the people that were back in Ireland,
sentences.zh: 这个词对某些人来说带有贬义，意指你的肩膀不像你的父母或留在爱尔兰的人那么宽阔，

sentences.en: that you weren't as strong.
sentences.zh: 意味着你没那么强壮。

sentences.en: Over the years, we would sit in the cafeteria and chat.
sentences.zh: 多年来，我们经常坐在食堂里聊天。

sentences.en: I would always approach him and he would say, Daniel, and I would say, James.
sentences.zh: 我总是走近他，他会说：“丹尼尔”，我会说：“詹姆斯”。

sentences.en: And we would sit down and commiserate about the inner politics at the New York Times or about the news of the day in New York City.
sentences.zh: 然后我们会坐下来，一起吐槽《纽约时报》内部的政治斗争，或者聊聊纽约市当天的新闻。

sentences.en: And often we would talk about Ireland.
sentences.zh: 我们还经常谈论爱尔兰。

sentences.en: He did a pretty good county-carry accent or brogue.
sentences.zh: 他能说一口相当地道的凯里郡口音或方言。

sentences.en: I never really tried.
sentences.zh: 我从来没试过。

sentences.en: I always sounded silly.
sentences.zh: 我学起来总显得很滑稽。

sentences.en: Jim died earlier this month after a very difficult battle with cancer.
sentences.zh: 本月初，吉姆在与癌症进行了非常艰难的抗争后去世了。

sentences.en: He was 63 years old.
sentences.zh: 他享年63岁。

sentences.en: And it seems like I've known him forever.
sentences.zh: 感觉我好像认识他一辈子了。

sentences.en: I was thinking even this morning about calling him about something.
sentences.zh: 今天早上我还在想，要不要就某件事给他打个电话。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm going to miss him.
sentences.zh: 是的，我会想念他的。

sentences.en: Now I'm going to read a piece by Jim that was written about a month after 9-11.
sentences.zh: 现在我要读一篇吉姆在“9·11”事件发生约一个月后写的文章。

sentences.en: And it appeared in a section that was dedicated to the reporting that followed the terrorist attack.
sentences.zh: 它发表在一个专门报道恐怖袭击后续事件的版面上。

sentences.en: It's called Fighting for Life, 50 Floors Up, with One Tool and Ingenuity.
sentences.zh: 标题是《在50层高空，仅凭一件工具和智慧，为生命而战》。

sentences.en: Now memories orbit around small things.
sentences.zh: 记忆往往围绕着细微的事物展开。

sentences.en: None of the other window washers liked his old green bucket.
sentences.zh: 其他擦窗工都不喜欢他那个旧绿桶。

sentences.en: But Jan Dempser, who worked inside one World Trade Center, found its rectangular mouth perfect for dipping and wetting his squeegee in one motion.
sentences.zh: 但曾在世界贸易中心一号楼内工作的简·登普瑟发现，它那长方形的桶口非常适合一次性完成浸水和润湿刮水板的动作。

sentences.en: So, on the morning of the 11th, as he waited at the 44th floor sky lobby to connect with elevators for higher floors,
sentences.zh: 因此，在11号那天早上，当他在44层的空中大厅等待换乘电梯前往更高楼层时，

sentences.en: Bucket and Squeegee dangled from the end of his arm.
sentences.zh: 水桶和刮水板正悬在他的手臂末端。

sentences.en: The time was 8.47.
sentences.zh: 时间是8点47分。

sentences.en: With five other men, Shivam Iyer, John Paskowski, George Phoenix, Colin Richardson, and another man, whose identity could not be learned, Mr. Dempser boarded car 69A,
sentences.zh: 登普瑟先生与另外五人——希瓦姆·艾耶、约翰·帕斯科夫斯基、乔治·菲尼克斯、科林·理查森，以及另一位身份不明的男士——登上了69A号电梯，

sentences.en: an express elevator that stopped on floors 67 through 74.
sentences.zh: 这是一部在67层到74层之间停靠的快速电梯。

sentences.en: The car rose, but before it reached its first landing, we felt a muted thud, Mr. Iyer said.
sentences.zh: 电梯上升了，但还没到达第一站，我们就感觉到了一声沉闷的撞击声，艾耶先生说。

sentences.en: The building shook.
sentences.zh: 大楼摇晃起来。

sentences.en: The elevator swung from side to side like a pendulum.
sentences.zh: 电梯像钟摆一样左右摇晃。

sentences.en: Then it plunged.
sentences.zh: 接着它坠落了。

sentences.en: In the car, someone punched an emergency stop button.
sentences.zh: 在电梯里，有人按下了紧急停止按钮。

sentences.en: At that moment, 8.48 a.m., one World Trade Center had entered the final 100 minutes of its existence.
sentences.zh: 那一刻，即上午8点48分，世界贸易中心一号楼进入了它存在的最后100分钟。

sentences.en: No one knew the clock was running, least of all the men trapped inside car 69A.
sentences.zh: 没人知道时钟已经在倒计时，尤其是被困在69A号电梯里的那些人。

sentences.en: They were as cut off 500 feet in the sky as if they had been trapped 500 feet underwater.
sentences.zh: 他们被困在500英尺的高空，与被困在水下500英尺并无两样。

sentences.en: They did not know their lives would depend on a simple tool.
sentences.zh: 他们不知道自己的生命将取决于一件简单的工具。

sentences.en: After 10 minutes, a live voice delivered a blunt message over the intercom.
sentences.zh: 10分钟后，对讲机里传来了一个生硬的声音。

sentences.en: There had been an explosion.
sentences.zh: 发生了一次爆炸。

sentences.en: Then the intercom went silent.
sentences.zh: 随后对讲机陷入了沉默。

sentences.en: Smoke seeped into the elevator cabin.
sentences.zh: 烟雾渗进了电梯轿厢。

sentences.en: One man cursed skyscrapers.
sentences.zh: 有人咒骂着摩天大楼。

sentences.en: Mr. Phoenix, the tallest, a Port Authority engineer, poked for a ceiling hatch.
sentences.zh: 个子最高的菲尼克斯先生，一位港务局工程师，在寻找天花板上的舱口。

sentences.en: Others pried apart the car doors, propping them open with the long wooden handle of Mr. Dempser's squeegee.
sentences.zh: 其他人撬开了电梯门，用登普瑟先生那把长长的木柄刮水板撑住门。

sentences.en: There was no exit.
sentences.zh: 没有出口。

sentences.en: They faced a wall stenciled with the number 50.
sentences.zh: 他们面对的是一堵印着数字“50”的墙。

sentences.en: That particular elevator bank did not serve the 50th floor, so there was no need for an opening.
sentences.zh: 那个特定的电梯组不服务50层，所以没必要开门。

sentences.en: To escape, they would have to make one themselves.
sentences.zh: 为了逃生，他们必须自己开一个出口。

sentences.en: Mr. Dempser felt the wall.
sentences.zh: 登普瑟先生摸了摸墙。

sentences.en: Sheet rock.
sentences.zh: 是石膏板。

sentences.en: Having worked in construction in his early days as a Polish immigrant, he knew that it could be cut with a sharp knife.
sentences.zh: 早年作为波兰移民从事建筑工作的他知道，这东西可以用锋利的刀切开。

sentences.en: No one had a knife.
sentences.zh: 但没人有刀。

sentences.en: From his bucket, Mr. Dempser drew his squeegee.
sentences.zh: 登普瑟先生从桶里拿出了他的刮水板。

sentences.en: He slid its metal edge against the wall, back and forth, over and over.
sentences.zh: 他将金属边缘抵在墙上，来回反复地刮擦。

sentences.en: He was spelled by the other men.
sentences.zh: 其他人轮流接替他。

sentences.en: Against the smoke, they breathed through handkerchiefs dampened in a container of milk Mr. Phoenix had just bought.
sentences.zh: 为了抵御烟雾，他们透过浸湿了菲尼克斯先生刚买的一盒牛奶的手帕呼吸。

sentences.en: Sheet rock comes in panels about one inch thick, Mr. Dempser recalled.
sentences.zh: 石膏板大约一英寸厚，登普瑟先生回忆道。

sentences.en: They cut an inch, then two inches.
sentences.zh: 他们切开了一英寸，然后是两英寸。

sentences.en: Mr. Dempser's hand ached.
sentences.zh: 登普瑟先生的手酸痛不已。

sentences.en: As he carved into the third panel, his hand shook.
sentences.zh: 当他切入第三层板时，他的手在颤抖。

sentences.en: He fumbled the squeegee, and it dropped down the shaft.
sentences.zh: 他不小心弄掉了刮水板，它掉进了电梯井里。

sentences.en: He had one tool left, a short metal squeegee handle.
sentences.zh: 他只剩下一件工具了，一个短小的金属刮水板手柄。

sentences.en: They carried on, with fists, feet, and handle, cutting in a regular rectangle about 12 by 18 inches.
sentences.zh: 他们继续用拳头、脚和手柄，切出一个大约12乘18英寸的长方形洞口。

sentences.en: Finally, they hid a layer of white tiles.
sentences.zh: 最后，他们露出了一层白瓷砖。

sentences.en: A bathroom.
sentences.zh: 那是间洗手间。

sentences.en: They broke the tiles.
sentences.zh: 他们砸碎了瓷砖。

sentences.en: One by one, the men squirmed through the opening, headfirst, sideways, popping onto the floor near a sink.
sentences.zh: 男人们一个接一个地从洞口钻了过去，头朝前，侧着身子，跳到了洗手池旁的地板上。

sentences.en: Mr. Dempser turned back.
sentences.zh: 登普瑟先生回过头。

sentences.en: I said, pass my bucket out, he recalled.
sentences.zh: 我说，把我的桶递出来，他回忆道。

sentences.en: By then, about 9.30, the 50th floor was already deserted, except for firefighters, astonished to see the six men emerge.
sentences.zh: 到那时，大约是9点30分，50层已经空无一人，除了消防员，他们惊讶地看到这六个人钻了出来。

sentences.en: I think it was Engine Company 5, Mr. Iyer said.
sentences.zh: 我想那是5号消防队，艾耶先生说。

sentences.en: They hustled us to the staircase.
sentences.zh: 他们催促我们去楼梯间。

sentences.en: On the excruciating, single-file descent through the smoke, someone teased Mr. Dempser about bringing his bucket.
sentences.zh: 在穿过烟雾、极其痛苦的单列撤离过程中，有人打趣登普瑟先生为什么要带着他的桶。

sentences.en: The company might not order me another one, he replied.
sentences.zh: 公司可能不会再给我配一个了，他回答道。

sentences.en: At the 15th floor, Mr. Iyer said, we heard a thunderous, metallic roar.
sentences.zh: 在15层，艾耶先生说，我们听到了一声雷鸣般的金属巨响。

sentences.en: I thought our lives had surely ended then.
sentences.zh: 我当时以为我们的生命肯定到头了。

sentences.en: The South Tower was collapsing.
sentences.zh: 南塔正在倒塌。

sentences.en: It was 9.59.
sentences.zh: 当时是9点59分。

sentences.en: Mr. Dempser dropped his bucket.
sentences.zh: 登普瑟先生丢下了他的桶。

sentences.en: The firefighters shouted to hurry.
sentences.zh: 消防员大喊着快点。

sentences.en: At 23 minutes past 10, they burst onto the street, ran for phones, sipped oxygen, and, five minutes later, fled as the North Tower collapsed.
sentences.zh: 10点23分，他们冲到了街上，跑去打电话，吸着氧气，五分钟后，随着北塔倒塌，他们四散逃离。

sentences.en: Their escape had taken 95 of the 100 minutes.
sentences.zh: 他们的逃生过程耗费了那100分钟里的95分钟。

sentences.en: It took up to one and a half minutes to clear each floor longer at the lower levels,
sentences.zh: 每下一层楼需要一分半钟，在低楼层则更久，

sentences.en: Mr. Iyer, an engineer with the board authority, said.
sentences.zh: 港务局的工程师艾耶先生说。

sentences.en: If the elevator had stopped at the 60th floor instead of the 50th, we would have been five minutes too late.
sentences.zh: 如果电梯停在60层而不是50层，我们就会晚五分钟。

sentences.en: And that man with the squeegee?
sentences.zh: 至于那个拿着刮水板的人？

sentences.en: He was like our guardian angel.
sentences.zh: 他就像我们的守护天使。

sentences.en: Since that day, Mr. Dempser has stayed home with his wife and children.
sentences.zh: 从那天起，登普瑟先生一直待在家里陪伴妻子和孩子。

sentences.en: He has pieced together the faces of the missing with the men and women he knew in the stations of his old life.
sentences.zh: 他将失踪者的面孔与他在旧生活中在车站认识的人拼凑在一起。

sentences.en: The security guard at the Japanese bank on the 93rd floor, who used to let him in at 6.30.
sentences.zh: 那位在93层日本银行工作的保安，以前总是6点30分让他进去。

sentences.en: The people at Car Futures on 92, the head of the port authority.
sentences.zh: 92层Car Futures公司的人，还有港务局的负责人。

sentences.en: Their faces keep him awake at night, he says.
sentences.zh: 他说，他们的面孔让他彻夜难眠。

sentences.en: His hands, the one that held the squeegee and the other that carried the bucket, shake with absence.
sentences.zh: 他的双手，那只握过刮水板的手和另一只提过水桶的手，因那种缺失感而颤抖。

sentences.en: Now I'm going to read a column by Jim about a police shooting in 1973 of a 10-year-old boy named Clifford Glover.
sentences.zh: 现在我要读一篇吉姆写的专栏，关于1973年一名警察枪杀了一名10岁男孩，名叫克利福德·格洛弗。

sentences.en: Jim wrote the column in 2015 after another police shooting in South Carolina, that of a man named Walter Scott.
sentences.zh: 吉姆是在2015年南卡罗来纳州发生另一起警察枪击案（受害者名叫沃尔特·斯科特）后写下这篇专栏的。

sentences.en: It's called A Police Shot to a Boy's Back in Queens, Echoing Since 1973.
sentences.zh: 标题是《皇后区男孩背部中弹，自1973年以来的回响》。

sentences.en: It was 1973, long before anyone could imagine hashtag declarations of solidarity and protest,
sentences.zh: 那是1973年，远在任何人能想象出用标签声明团结和抗议之前，

sentences.en: the kind of message to the world that today might read, hashtag, I am Clifford Glover in the fourth grade.
sentences.zh: 那种今天可能会写成“#我是四年级的克利福德·格洛弗”这样传达给世界的信息。

sentences.en: No one could pull out a phone to make a video of Clifford Glover, a 10-year-old running from a plainclothes police officer with a gun,
sentences.zh: 当时没人能掏出手机拍下克利福德·格洛弗的视频，这个10岁的孩子正在躲避一名持枪的便衣警察，

sentences.en: who had just jumped out of a white Buick Skylark in Jamaica, Queens on a spring morning in 1973.
sentences.zh: 那名警察在1973年春天的早晨，刚从牙买加皇后区的一辆白色别克Skylark车里跳出来。

sentences.en: I am sure a camera would have helped, but the ballistics were clear,
sentences.zh: 我相信如果有摄像头会有帮助，但弹道分析很清楚，

sentences.en: Albert Gaudeli, a former Queens prosecutor, said this week.
sentences.zh: 前皇后区检察官阿尔伯特·高德利本周表示。

sentences.en: The bullet entered his lower back and came out at the top of his cheSt.
sentences.zh: 子弹从他的后腰射入，从胸部上方穿出。

sentences.en: He was shot T-square in the back, with his body leaning forward.
sentences.zh: 他背部正中一枪，当时身体正向前倾。

sentences.en: He was running away.
sentences.zh: 他在逃跑。

sentences.en: That bullet killed Clifford Glover.
sentences.zh: 那颗子弹杀死了克利福德·格洛弗。

sentences.en: Its trajectory, through a family, a neighborhood, a generation, can be traced to this day in injuries that never healed, in a story with no final word.
sentences.zh: 它穿过一个家庭、一个社区、一代人的轨迹，至今仍能从那些从未愈合的伤口中，从一个没有结局的故事里追溯出来。

sentences.en: When a black man named Walter Scott was shot by a white police officer in North Charleston, South Carolina, on April 4th,
sentences.zh: 当一名叫沃尔特·斯科特的黑人男子于4月4日在南卡罗来纳州北查尔斯顿被一名白人警察枪杀时，

sentences.en: a cell phone video made by a passerby showed that Mr. Scott was also running away when he was killed and that he was not, as the police officer claimed, carrying a police taser.
sentences.zh: 路人拍摄的手机视频显示，斯科特先生被杀时也在逃跑，而且他并没有像警察声称的那样携带警用泰瑟枪。

sentences.en: With all this killing and stuff, said Pauline Armstead, a sister of the dead boy, they need to go back to Cliffy Glover.
sentences.zh: “伴随着所有这些杀戮之类的事情，”死者男孩的姐姐宝琳·阿姆斯特德说，“他们需要回过头来看看克利福德·格洛弗的案子。”

sentences.en: Clifford, a black boy, had been shot by Officer Thomas Shea, a white man, who said he had tried to question him and his stepfather because they fit the descriptions of cab robbers.
sentences.zh: 克利福德是一个黑人男孩，被白人警察托马斯·谢伊枪杀，谢伊声称他试图盘问男孩和他的继父，因为他们符合出租车抢劫案嫌疑人的特征。

sentences.en: They ran.
sentences.zh: 他们跑了。

sentences.en: The officer said he fired when Clifford, in flight, pointed a gun at him, which the mortally injured boy had then managed to toss or hand to his stepfather.
sentences.zh: 警察说，当克利福德在逃跑时用枪指着他，他才开火，而那个受了致命伤的男孩随后设法把枪扔掉或交给了继父。

sentences.en: In the hours and days that followed the shooting, armies of investigators scoured the streets and sewers,
sentences.zh: 在枪击事件发生后的几天里，大批调查人员搜查了街道和下水道，

sentences.en: poured over court records, and arrived, without warrants, to search the homes of Clifford's family and relatives.
sentences.zh: 翻阅了法庭记录，并在没有搜查令的情况下闯入克利福德家人和亲戚的家中进行搜查。

sentences.en: Guys were trying to help Shea and coming up with all kinds of stuff, said Mr. Gordelli, who was the chief homicide prosecutor in Queens at the time.
sentences.zh: “当时有些人试图帮谢伊脱罪，编造了各种各样的东西，”时任皇后区首席凶杀案检察官的高德利先生说。

sentences.en: Someone showed up with a starter's pistol, but as soon as he pressed them on it, they folded.
sentences.zh: 有人拿出一把发令枪，但当他一追问，他们就露馅了。

sentences.en: There was no gun.
sentences.zh: 根本没有枪。

sentences.en: People in Jamaica rose in proteSt.
sentences.zh: 牙买加社区的民众奋起抗议。

sentences.en: The streets were blocked with heavy construction equipment owned by a black contractor.
sentences.zh: 街道被一名黑人承包商拥有的重型建筑设备封锁了。

sentences.en: Mr. Shea became the first police officer in nearly 50 years to be charged with committing murder while on duty.
sentences.zh: 谢伊先生成为近50年来第一位被指控在执勤期间犯下谋杀罪的警察。

sentences.en: Shea says that the kid turned and appeared to have a gun, Mr. Gordelli said.
sentences.zh: “谢伊说那个孩子转过身，看起来有枪，”高德利先生说。

sentences.en: That's what got him indicted.
sentences.zh: 这就是他被起诉的原因。

sentences.en: The ballistics made Shea a liar.
sentences.zh: 弹道证据证明谢伊是个骗子。

sentences.en: But not apparently a murderer.
sentences.zh: 但显然不是谋杀犯。

sentences.en: At least in the eyes of the jury of 11 white men and one black woman who found him not guilty.
sentences.zh: 至少在由11名白人男性和1名黑人女性组成的陪审团眼中，他们裁定他无罪。

sentences.en: Afterward, many of the jurors joined Mr. Shea and his lawyers at a Queens Boulevard restaurant to celebrate.
sentences.zh: 事后，许多陪审员加入了谢伊先生及其律师的行列，在皇后大道的一家餐厅庆祝。

sentences.en: They told reporters it was possible Mr. Shea had been telling the truth about seeing a gun.
sentences.zh: 他们告诉记者，谢伊先生关于看到枪的说法可能是真的。

sentences.en: That same day, word of the verdict reached a baseball field on the grounds of the South Jamaica Houses, known locally as the Forty Projects.
sentences.zh: 就在同一天，裁决的消息传到了南牙买加住宅区（当地人称为“四十号项目”）内的一个棒球场。

sentences.en: Eric Adams, who was then a 13-year-old from the neighborhood, was waiting to bat.
sentences.zh: 当时13岁的社区少年埃里克·亚当斯正在等待击球。

sentences.en: We were playing a Long Island team that happened to be all white, said Mr. Adams, who became a police officer and is now the Brooklyn Borough president.
sentences.zh: 亚当斯先生说，当时我们正在和一支来自长岛的球队比赛，那支球队恰好全是白人。亚当斯先生后来成为了一名警官，现在是布鲁克林区区长。

sentences.en: When the news came out, about 200 people emerged on the field.
sentences.zh: 消息传出后，大约200人涌上了球场。

sentences.en: They just took the baseball bats and started beating the white players, chanting,
sentences.zh: 他们直接拿起棒球棍开始殴打那些白人球员，并高喊着，

sentences.en: Shea got away.
sentences.zh: 谢伊逃脱了。

sentences.en: Later, Mr. Shea would be fired despite a rally by police officers and the pleas of his lawyer, Jacob Evserov, who said his client was needed on the force, quote,
sentences.zh: 后来，尽管有警官们举行集会声援，还有他的律师雅各布·埃夫塞罗夫的恳求，谢伊先生还是被解雇了。律师称他的当事人是警队所必需的，引用原话：

sentences.en: to protect us from the animals who roam the streets of New York, end quote.
sentences.zh: “为了保护我们免受那些在纽约街头游荡的野兽的伤害”，引用结束。

sentences.en: The Long Island baseball team had come to Queens as part of an interracial inter-neighborhood thing, Mr. Adams said.
sentences.zh: 亚当斯先生说，那支长岛棒球队来到皇后区是作为跨种族、跨社区交流活动的一部分。

sentences.en: It was their first visit.
sentences.zh: 那是他们第一次来访。

sentences.en: The Jamaica team tried to stop the assault but could not.
sentences.zh: 牙买加队的队员试图阻止这场袭击，但没能成功。

sentences.en: That was all the outrage, he said, adding that because of what happened, a lot of our guys quit the team, never played baseball again.
sentences.zh: 他说，这就是所有的愤怒所在，并补充道，因为发生了这件事，我们队里的很多人都退出了，再也没有打过棒球。

sentences.en: For his generation of black boys and girls, Mr. Adams said, the verdict brought a lot of despair.
sentences.zh: 亚当斯先生说，对于他那一代的黑人男孩和女孩来说，这个判决带来了极大的绝望。

sentences.en: The year after Clifford Glover died, the number of shots fired by officers declined by nearly half.
sentences.zh: 克利福德·格洛弗去世后的那一年，警官开枪的次数减少了近一半。

sentences.en: In 2013, the number of shots fired was 248, the fewest since the police department began keeping detailed records in 1971.
sentences.zh: 2013年，开枪次数为248次，是自1971年警察局开始详细记录以来的最低值。

sentences.en: At the peak, in 1972, officers fired 2,510 bullets.
sentences.zh: 在1972年的高峰期，警官们发射了2510发子弹。

sentences.en: Because Mr. Shea had spoken freely with his superiors, the largest police union began a campaign, urging its members not to talk after a shooting until a union lawyer had arrived.
sentences.zh: 由于谢伊先生曾与上级坦诚交谈，最大的警察工会发起了一场运动，敦促其成员在发生枪击事件后，在工会律师到达之前不要开口说话。

sentences.en: For Clifford's family, his death changed everything.
sentences.zh: 对于克利福德的家人来说，他的死改变了一切。

sentences.en: They wrote that we were poor, Darlene Armstead, a younger sister, said this week.
sentences.zh: 妹妹达琳·阿姆斯特德本周说，他们写道我们很穷。

sentences.en: As she and three other siblings, Kenneth, Pauline, and Patricia Armstead, described the household this week,
sentences.zh: 当她和另外三个兄弟姐妹——肯尼斯、波琳和帕特里夏·阿姆斯特德——本周描述这个家庭时，

sentences.en: the family may not have had much money, but before Clifford's killing, it was sound.
sentences.zh: 他们说，这个家庭可能没有多少钱，但在克利福德被杀之前，它是健全的。

sentences.en: Darlene's father, Ad Armstead, who was Clifford's stepfather, went to work every morning at a junkyard.
sentences.zh: 达琳的父亲阿德·阿姆斯特德，也就是克利福德的继父，每天早上都去垃圾场工作。

sentences.en: The family had dinner each night at the same time around one table, Ms. Armstead said, then watched cowboy shows on television.
sentences.zh: 阿姆斯特德女士说，全家人每天晚上都在同一时间围着一张桌子吃晚饭，然后看电视上的牛仔节目。

sentences.en: On summer weekends, neighborhood children feasted in the backyard on watermelon laid out on a door covered by a sheet that rested on two clean garbage cans.
sentences.zh: 在夏天的周末，邻居家的孩子们会在后院享用西瓜，西瓜放在一张盖着床单的门板上，门板架在两个干净的垃圾桶上。

sentences.en: Ad Armstead and his brothers enjoyed cigars and burgers.
sentences.zh: 阿德·阿姆斯特德和他的兄弟们喜欢抽雪茄和吃汉堡。

sentences.en: My father taught us structure, Darlene Armstead said.
sentences.zh: 达琳·阿姆斯特德说，我父亲教导我们要有条理。

sentences.en: She had to make beds.
sentences.zh: 她必须整理床铺。

sentences.en: One brother had to clean the yard and bring out the garbage.
sentences.zh: 一个兄弟必须打扫院子并把垃圾拿出去。

sentences.en: Clifford, a fourth grader at public school 40, went with his stepfather on weekends to the junkyard, carrying his own little wrench.
sentences.zh: 克利福德是公立学校40分校的四年级学生，周末他会带着自己的小扳手和继父一起去垃圾场。

sentences.en: On the morning of April 28th, 1973, a Saturday, Ad Armstead woke Clifford before dawn so they could be at the yard to move cranes into place for a delivery.
sentences.zh: 1973年4月28日，一个星期六的早晨，阿德·阿姆斯特德在黎明前叫醒了克利福德，这样他们就能赶到垃圾场，把起重机移到位置以便送货。

sentences.en: They walked a few blocks along New York Boulevard, known today as Guy R.
sentences.zh: 他们沿着纽约大道走了几个街区，也就是今天所说的盖伊·R·

sentences.en: Brewer Boulevard, when an unmarked car pulled alongside them.
sentences.zh: 布鲁尔大道，这时一辆无标志的汽车停在他们旁边。

sentences.en: Mr. Armstead, carrying wages that he had been paid the day before, said he and Clifford ran, afraid that they were going to be robbed.
sentences.zh: 阿姆斯特德先生带着前一天领到的工资，说他和克利福德跑开了，因为害怕会被抢劫。

sentences.en: Hearing shots, he flagged down a patrol car, not realizing that Clifford had been felled.
sentences.zh: 听到枪声，他拦下了一辆巡逻车，却没意识到克利福德已经被击倒了。

sentences.en: Mr. Shea testified that he did not realize that Clifford, who stood just five feet tall and weighed less than 100 pounds, was a child.
sentences.zh: 谢伊先生作证说，他没有意识到克利福德是个孩子，他身高只有五英尺，体重不到100磅。

sentences.en: After the shooting, prosecutors said, Mr. Shea's partner, Walter Scott, was recorded on a radio transmission saying, die, you little, adding an expletive.
sentences.zh: 检察官说，枪击事件发生后，谢伊先生的搭档沃尔特·斯科特在无线电传输中被录下说，去死吧，你这个小杂种，并加了一个脏话。

sentences.en: Mr. Scott denied it was his voice.
sentences.zh: 斯科特先生否认那是他的声音。

sentences.en: Clifford's death sent his mother, Eloise Glover, into a tailspin.
sentences.zh: 克利福德的死让他的母亲埃洛伊丝·格洛弗陷入了崩溃。

sentences.en: My mother turned on my father.
sentences.zh: 我母亲开始针对我父亲。

sentences.en: Did you have a gun?
sentences.zh: 你当时有枪吗？

sentences.en: They said you had a gun, Darlene Armstead said.
sentences.zh: 达琳·阿姆斯特德说，他们说你有枪。

sentences.en: It caused them to break up.
sentences.zh: 这导致他们分手了。

sentences.en: My mother lost her mind.
sentences.zh: 我母亲疯了。

sentences.en: The family received a settlement from New York City that, in the memory of the children, came to about $50,000, most of which the mother lent to local churches, but never got back.
sentences.zh: 这家人从纽约市获得了一笔赔偿金，在孩子们的记忆中大约有5万美元，母亲把大部分钱借给了当地的教堂，但再也没要回来。

sentences.en: My mother didn't want no one to know when she was going outside, Ms. Armstead said.
sentences.zh: 阿姆斯特德女士说，我母亲不想让任何人知道她什么时候出门。

sentences.en: She always used the back door.
sentences.zh: 她总是走后门。

sentences.en: Ms. Armstead recalled sleeping nights on chairs in hospital emergency rooms while her mother was being treated and living off restaurant handouts.
sentences.zh: 阿姆斯特德女士回忆起母亲接受治疗时，她晚上睡在医院急诊室的椅子上，靠餐馆的施舍生活。

sentences.en: She was going to pay this guy to board up the house, and she would pay him to bring the food to us, she said.
sentences.zh: 她说，她打算付钱给那个家伙把房子封起来，并付钱让他把食物带给我们。

sentences.en: The children went to foster care and group homes.
sentences.zh: 孩子们被送进了寄养家庭和集体宿舍。

sentences.en: One brother was in a psychiatric institution for about 10 years.
sentences.zh: 一个兄弟在精神病院住了大约10年。

sentences.en: Her mother, who had diabetes, died in 1990 at age 54.
sentences.zh: 她患有糖尿病的母亲于1990年去世，享年54岁。

sentences.en: Add Armstead died in 2005 at 83.
sentences.zh: 阿德·阿姆斯特德于2005年去世，享年83岁。

sentences.en: They put guns on him.
sentences.zh: 他们把枪栽赃给他。

sentences.en: They said he had guns at work, at home, Kenneth Armstead said.
sentences.zh: 肯尼斯·阿姆斯特德说，他们说他在工作时、在家里都有枪。

sentences.en: To demonize him would help Shea's story.
sentences.zh: 妖魔化他有助于谢伊的故事。

sentences.en: Mr. Shea, who moved out of the state after his marriage broke up, could not be reached.
sentences.zh: 谢伊先生在婚姻破裂后搬离了该州，无法联系到他。

sentences.en: I've lost it all, he told the author Thomas Hauser, whose 1980 book,
sentences.zh: 他告诉作家托马斯·豪泽，我失去了一切，豪泽1980年的书，

sentences.en: The Trial of Patrolman Thomas Shea, is a comprehensive account of the episode.
sentences.zh: 《托马斯·谢伊警官的审判》，是对这一事件的全面记录。

sentences.en: The defense lawyer, Mr. Evserov, said a video would have changed nothing.
sentences.zh: 辩护律师埃夫塞罗夫先生说，视频什么也改变不了。

sentences.en: The case was resolved as a result of a trial, he said.
sentences.zh: 他说，案件是通过审判解决的。

sentences.en: For Mr. Adams, the quick termination of the South Carolina police officer in the shooting this month of Walter Scott was a positive step.
sentences.zh: 对于亚当斯先生来说，本月南卡罗来纳州警官在枪杀沃尔特·斯科特后被迅速解雇，是一个积极的步骤。

sentences.en: That mayor said, you know what, it has just gone too far, Mr. Adams said.
sentences.zh: 亚当斯先生说，那位市长说，你知道吗，这太过分了。

sentences.en: The pathway of Shea's bullet physically stopped when it hit Clifford Glover.
sentences.zh: 谢伊子弹的轨迹在击中克利福德·格洛弗时在物理上停止了。

sentences.en: But the emotional pathway probably still continues to this day.
sentences.zh: 但情感的轨迹可能至今仍在延续。

sentences.en: This was recorded by the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 这是由《纽约时报》录制的。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Dan Barry.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢丹·巴里。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·朗森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一个关于热爱设计及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs, in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you
sentences.zh: 即使在我还在夜总会当DJ的时候，在黑胶唱片时代，你每天晚上都要带着300件你最珍贵的财产去上班，

sentences.en: and you turned a DJ booth into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你把DJ台变成了一个活生生的、充满50年历史精美文物的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: As a host as Samuels, aahltino, a
sentences.zh: 作为主持人萨缪尔斯，阿尔蒂诺，一个
